Enacted · PP 33/2026
PP Pasal 10
PP Pasal 10

Pihak dalam pemrosesan Data Pribadi yang diatur dalam Peraturan Pemerintah ini terdiri atas:

  1. a.
    Subjek Data Pribadi;
  2. b.
    Pengendali Data Pribadi; dan/atau
  3. c.
    Prosesor Data Pribadi.
What changed

RPP Pasal 16 ayat (3) deemed any party requesting personal data to be a controller. PP Pasal 10 lists the three parties to processing that the Regulation governs and carries no such deeming rule. The other limb survives: the rule in RPP Pasal 16 ayat (2) sits in the definitions at PP Pasal 1 angka 6, so it is not deleted.

Analysis

The draft resolved the status of a party demanding personal data; the enacted text does not. RPP Pasal 16 ayat (3) fixed controller responsibility on recipients who never handled the data themselves, which mattered most for group companies, platforms and public bodies issuing data requests.

PP Pasal 10 lists the parties and stops there, so controller status on inbound and outbound data requests now follows from the functional definition at PP Pasal 1 angka 4 alone, which turns on who determines the purpose and exercises control over the processing. The other limb of RPP Pasal 16 is intact.

Its ayat (2) states the same rule as PP Pasal 1 angka 6, so the data subject is defined once in the definitions article instead of being restated in the article on parties. The deeming rule is the limb with no counterpart in the enacted article.

What to do about it

Assign controller status expressly in data sharing agreements because the Regulation no longer deems the requesting party a controller.

Where Europe stands diverges GDPR Articles 2, 4

The provision. GDPR Article 4(7) defines a controller functionally, as the natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which alone or jointly with others determines the purposes and means of processing.

Against Indonesia. Both texts reach much the same set of addressees by different routes.

What changed

The draft scope list included the powers of the Lembaga PDP and dispute resolution together with procedural law. The enacted list replaces those with public participation and supervision of controller compliance, and narrows the transfer head to transfers out of Indonesian jurisdiction.

Analysis

The scope list records the structural rearrangement between the two texts. The draft's Chapter VII on the powers of the Lembaga PDP has no counterpart chapter in the enacted text: its supervision section at RPP Articles 203 to 205 returns as Chapter VIII at PP 33/2026 Articles 180 to 183, while its policy making, law enforcement assistance and public interest litigation sections have no enacted home at all.

Procedural law drops out of the scope list and out of the chapter title, and PP 33/2026 Pasal 200(2) sends the hukum acara to the general law, even though the dispute chapter itself grows from RPP Articles 227 to 244 to PP 33/2026 Articles 200 to 222 and keeps the mediation procedure in detail. A reader looking for the authority's investigative and decision making powers must now assemble them from Chapters VIII and IX rather than from a dedicated chapter.

What to do about it

Do not cite draft Chapter VII; the authority's powers now sit across Chapters VIII and IX.

Where Europe stands diverges GDPR Articles 2, 3

The provision. GDPR Article 2 sets material scope: processing wholly or partly by automated means, plus non-automated processing of data in a filing system.

Against Indonesia. The extraterritorial trigger differs on both sides.

Final provisions

The draft applied on promulgation and the enacted text waited

clock changedchanges an obligation
Draft · 31 August 2023
RPP Pasal 245
RPP Pasal 245

Peraturan Pemerintah ini mulai berlaku pada tanggal diundangkan.

Enacted · PP 33/2026
PP Pasal 225
PP Pasal 225

Peraturan Pemerintah ini mulai berlaku setelah 6 (enam) bulan terhitung sejak tanggal diundangkan.

What changed

Immediate application became a six-month delay, which places the commencement date at 16 January 2027.

Analysis

Had the draft been adopted as it stood, all 245 articles would have bound every controller on the day of promulgation. The enacted text grants six months from the 16 July 2026 promulgation recorded in Pasal 225, and Pasal 223 adds a second cushion by allowing processing to continue so long as it does not conflict with this regulation until the Peraturan Lembaga on processing are issued.

Pasal 224 holds existing personal data legislation in force on the same non-conflict test. Thirty four articles across the instrument defer a mechanism to a Peraturan Lembaga, and the twelve on cooperation, public participation, supervision, sanctions and disputes fall outside the Pasal 223 cushion.

What to do about it

16 January 2027 is the date. Pasal 223 is what you rely on for processing rules not yet issued.

Where Europe stands diverges GDPR Articles 94, 99

The provision. GDPR Article 99(1) sets entry into force at the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal, which was 24 May 2016.

Against Indonesia. GDPR Article 99 separates two dates that UU Pasal 76 keeps together.

Final provisions

Transitional article added for the gap before Lembaga rules

newchanges an obligation
Draft · 31 August 2023
no counterpart

The draft had no such provision.

Enacted · PP 33/2026
PP Pasal 223
PP Pasal 223

Sampai dengan ditetapkannya Peraturan Lembaga terkait pemrosesan Data Pribadi, Pengendali Data Pribadi dan/atau Prosesor Data Pribadi melakukan pemrosesan Data Pribadi sepanjang tidak bertentangan dengan ketentuan Peraturan Pemerintah ini.

What changed

The draft had no transitional provision for controllers. The enacted text adds Pasal 223, allowing processing to continue until the Peraturan Lembaga on processing are issued so long as it does not conflict with the regulation, and Pasal 224 saves existing personal data legislation on the same condition.

Analysis

The draft left twenty four matters to a Peraturan Lembaga PDP without saying what governed in the interval, so a controller reading it had no answer for the period before those rules appeared. Pasal 223 closes that gap by making the regulation itself the interim standard, and Pasal 224 preserves existing personal data rules to the extent they are consistent.

The condition is conflict with this regulation, not conflict with a future Peraturan Lembaga, so the yardstick for the interim period is the enacted text alone. What remains unoperationalised is the test for conflict, which no provision defines.

What to do about it

Map current processing against the enacted articles rather than waiting for Peraturan Lembaga, because Pasal 223 makes the regulation the interim benchmark.

The provision. GDPR Article 99 has two paragraphs.

Against Indonesia. Both instruments buy two years, in different places.

Where Europe stands

The four relations, and what we have read to say so

Every GDPR panel in the tracker is written from two corpora held on disk, the EDPB guidance and the judgments of the Court of Justice. These slides turn that index around: start from a guideline or a judgment and see which articles of UU 27/2022 it bears on.

ported from the GDPR

The Indonesian wording or structure tracks the GDPR closely enough to read as a transposition.

9 articles
aligned

The same protective work is done, by a route of its own rather than by the GDPR mechanism.

5 articles
diverges

The mechanism, the threshold or the actor differs, so the same words do not produce the same result.

61 articles
no GDPR counterpart

The article has no counterpart in the GDPR at all.

1 articles
Why so many diverge

The count is not a verdict on the statute. Most of it records a structural fact: the GDPR carries its detail in the Regulation, and UU 27/2022 carries much of its detail in PP 33/2026 and in the Peraturan Lembaga still to come, so the two texts rarely put the same rule in the same place.

Where Europe stands

State access, and the test an adequacy assessment runs

The instrument

Recommendations 02/2020 on the European Essential Guarantees for surveillance measures, adopted 10 November 2020, sets out four European Essential Guarantees. A third country regime has to meet all four before an interference with privacy can be treated as justified.

The four guarantees

Processing on clear, precise and accessible rules. Necessity and proportionality actually demonstrated. An independent oversight mechanism. An effective remedy available to the individual. They are drawn from the case law rather than from the Regulation, which is why the judgments below are cited by no article of the statute.

Where it bites in this deck

The state access findings in this comparison, the lost attachment requirement, the widened signing authority and the deleted requester identity limbs, are exactly what Guarantee A and Guarantee C ask about. The exception regime sits at UU Pasal 15 and UU Pasal 50, the transfer cascade at UU Pasal 56.

What is not here

No decision of a national supervisory authority is cited anywhere: the obvious source sits behind a proof of work wall, and getting around bot detection is not something this project does. Three EDPB adequacy opinions are served as damaged files and are recorded as unverified, with nothing cited from them.

Where this comes from

Every clause on these slides was checked against both texts

Method

Both instruments were parsed to article level and matched by subject matter rather than by number, because numbering did not survive: of 321 comparable pairs only around 36 carried across almost word for word. Each quotation was then verified mechanically against the source files, and any claimed difference that turned out to be a provision which had merely moved was discarded.

Sources

UU No. 27 of 2022 and PP No. 33 of 2026, official copies, both linked article by article in the full tracker. The 2023 draft is a working document and is cited by article without a link.
